[3, 6] During the first race of the weekend on October 21, Spain's Marta García clinched the inaugural F1 Academy drivers' title. [5, 9] The calendar for the 2023 season, including the Austin finale, was announced on February 23, 2023. [3, 4, 6] An F1 Academy round in Miami was later scheduled for the subsequent 2024 season and announced on October 17, 2023. [1, 2] This partnership includes Gulf's branding on the new FW45 car, race driver suits, and pitstop equipment, and extends to the Williams Racing Driver Academy and Williams Esports. [1, 2] Simultaneously, the team revealed a regional partnership with the American beer brand Michelob ULTRA, making it the team's Official North American Beer Partner for the 2023 season. [3, 11] This collaboration is set to provide premier experiences for fans at the North American Grands Prix and includes Michelob ULTRA branding on the FW45 and driver race suits at those specific events. [2, 16] The American automaker is entering into a long-term strategic technical partnership with Red Bull Powertrains to develop a new hybrid power unit for the 2026 Formula 1 season. [2, 9] This collaboration, named Red Bull Ford Powertrains, will supply power units to both the Oracle Red Bull Racing and Scuderia AlphaTauri teams from 2026 until at least 2030. [2, 9] The new power unit will align with the 2026 regulations, which mandate a 350kW electric motor and a combustion engine capable of using fully sustainable fuels. [2, 8] Ford will contribute its expertise in areas such as battery cell and electric motor technology, as well as power unit control software and analytics. [2] <6> Oracle Red Bull Racing held its 2023 season launch in New York City on February 3, 2023, where it unveiled the livery for its new RB19 car. [3, 5, 6] The event, which took place at the Classic Car Club Manhattan, marked the first time a Formula 1 team had ever held its season launch in the United States. [3, 8] In addition to the car's livery reveal, the team made a significant announcement regarding a future technical partnership with Ford, which will commence in 2026. [2, 3] This collaboration will see Ford partner with Red Bull Powertrains to develop the next-generation hybrid power unit for the new regulations. [2] The launch event was attended by Team Principal Christian Horner, drivers Max Verstappen and Sergio Pérez, and the team's new third driver, Daniel Ricciardo. [3, 7] Red Bull also launched a fan-focused initiative called 'Make Your Mark', a competition allowing fans to design the car's livery for the three US Grands Prix in 2023. [8, 11] <7> The MoneyGram Haas F1 Team, the sole American-owned team in Formula 1, digitally unveiled the new livery for its VF-23 car on January 31, 2023. This was the first livery reveal of all ten F1 teams for the 2023 season. The design, rendered in a mix of red, white, and black, prominently featured the branding of its new US-based title sponsor, MoneyGram. Team Principal Guenther Steiner noted the design was a "more elevated and modernized look" fit for the new partnership era. The physical VF-23 car had its first shakedown at Silverstone Circuit on February 11, 2023, ahead of the official pre-season testing in Bahrain.

The impact caused extensive damage to Sainz's car, affecting the chassis, engine, and battery, and also damaged Esteban Ocon's Alpine, which required a chassis change. Following the incident, race officials conducted a thorough inspection of all similar covers on the 3.85-mile street circuit, leading to a multi-hour delay. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> Williams Racing officially announced on December 1, 2023, that American driver Logan Sargeant's contract had been extended, securing his position with the team for the 2024 Formula 1 season. [1, 2, 3] This announcement was significant as it filled the final vacant seat, thereby completing the entire 20-driver grid for the 2024 F1 World Championship. [6] The confirmation meant that for the first time in Formula 1 history, the driver lineup at the end of one season would be identical at the start of the next. [6] Sargeant's renewal came after a rookie season where he became the first American in 30 years to score a point in F1. [1, 2] <2> Williams Racing officially confirmed on December 1, 2023, that American driver Logan Sargeant would continue to race for the team in the 2024 Formula 1 season. This announcement solidified the 2024 F1 grid, with Sargeant being the last driver to have his seat confirmed. The decision came after his rookie season, in which he became the first American F1 driver to score a point in 30 years with a 10th place finish at the United States Grand Prix. Prediction target period: from 2024-05-12 to 2024-07-28. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> A bipartisan group of 12 U.S. Congress members sent a letter to Liberty Media, the commercial rights holder for Formula 1, regarding the rejection of Andretti Global's entry into the F1 championship. [1, 2] The letter, dated May 1, 2024, and addressed to Liberty's CEO Greg Maffei, voices concerns about "apparent anti-competitive actions" that could be preventing Andretti and its partner, General Motors (GM), from joining the grid. [2, 3] The lawmakers question the authority and rationale behind the rejection by Formula One Management (FOM), suggesting the decision appears to be driven by a desire to protect the existing European-based teams from American competition. [2, 8] Citing the Sherman Antitrust Act, the letter questions how the denial complies with U.S. law and requests a response by May 3, 2024. [3, 5, 6] <2> Formula 1 announced the launch of a free, 24/7 ad-supported streaming channel in the United States, named the 'Formula 1 Channel'. The channel, operated by C15 Studio, aims to enhance the fan experience and attract new audiences in the growing U.S. market by complementing the live broadcasts on ESPN and F1 TV. Content includes race replays and highlights from Formula 1, F2, F3, and F1 Academy, which are made available five days after each event, alongside classic Grand Prix reruns and documentaries. The service was scheduled to go live on Amazon Freevee and Pluto TV starting May 1, 2024, with a launch on Samsung TV Plus to follow on May 10, strategically preceding the Miami Grand Prix. <3> The third annual Racing Fan Fest, presented by SWARM Entertainment Group, took place from May 2 to May 5, 2024, at the Wynwood Marketplace, located at 2250 NW Second Avenue in Miami. This large, free-to-the-public, off-track festival coincided with the Formula 1 Miami Grand Prix week. The four-day event featured a variety of attractions for racing enthusiasts and families, including an immersive Red Bull Fan Zone. Highlights included racing simulators that allowed attendees to virtually drive the Miami Grand Prix track, a pit stop challenge, and car displays featuring the Oracle Red Bull Racing RB20 and the Visa Cash App RB Formula One Team's RB01. The festival also offered live music from DJs such as Ariel Assault and Kaos, curated pop-up shops from brands like Hugo Boss and New Era, and a food and beverage village with local vendors. All practice, qualifying, and race sessions were live-streamed at the event. <4> The 2025 Formula 1 Crypto.com Miami Grand Prix is confirmed to take place at the Miami International Autodrome in Miami Gardens, Florida. The event is scheduled for the weekend of May 2-4, 2025, with the main race on Sunday, May 4, 2025. It will be the sixth round of the 24-race 2025 Formula One World Championship. The Grand Prix will also be the second of six events in the season to feature the sprint format. The official 2025 F1 calendar was announced by the FIA and Formula 1 on April 12, 2024. <5> Andretti Global has officially opened a new, 48,000-square-foot facility at Silverstone Park, UK, as it continues its preparations for a potential Formula 1 entry. [3, 5] Despite a prior rejection from Formula One Management (FOM) for the 2026 season, the American team is proceeding with its plans by establishing this European base in the UK's 'Motorsport Valley' to attract top F1 talent and build out its infrastructure. [5, 6, 8] The new facility, which was inaugurated by Michael and Mario Andretti, will house manufacturing facilities, research and development, and office space for its approximately 80 UK-based employees. [3, 6] This site will work in conjunction with Andretti's main US headquarters in Indiana and the GM Tech Center in North Carolina. [3] The team's persistence signals a strong commitment to eventually joining the F1 grid, with FOM potentially reconsidering their application for a 2028 entry. [8] <6> Red Bull Racing announced that Ford Motor Company will be the title partner for its entry in the 2024 F1 Academy season, the all-female racing series. The team, now known as the Red Bull Ford Academy Programme, aims to cultivate female racing talent and help them progress to higher levels of motorsport. The partnership includes prominent Ford branding on the car, team apparel, and the driver's gear, which for the 2024 season is Emely de Heus. The collaboration is an extension of Red Bull's efforts to foster diversity and inclusion in motorsport and marks a significant step in providing a pathway for female drivers to realize their potential. The partnership officially debuted at the first race of the F1 Academy season in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. <7> The Visa Cash App RB Formula One team officially unveiled its 2024 contender, the VCARB-01, at a launch event in Las Vegas on February 8, 2024. [2, 3, 16] The new car's livery is a notable departure from its predecessor, AlphaTauri, featuring a striking blue and white design with red accents that pays homage to the team's Toro Rosso history. [6, 12, 14] The design prominently features branding from new American title sponsors, Visa and Cash App, signifying a new commercial era for the team. [9] The launch event, which included a performance by Pulitzer Prize-winning artist Kendrick Lamar, was attended by drivers Daniel Ricciardo and Yuki Tsunoda, alongside team CEO Peter Bayer and Team Principal Laurent Mekies. [3, 6] <8> The MoneyGram Haas F1 Team, the sole American team in Formula 1, revealed the design and livery for its VF-24 challenger on February 2, 2024, ahead of the FIA Formula 1 World Championship. The unveiling was conducted digitally, with a series of renders released across the team's social media platforms. This marked the first car design reveal for the 2024 season. The VF-24's livery is an evolution of the previous year's design, featuring a predominantly black color scheme with red and white accents. The team announced that the car's physical debut would be during a shakedown at Silverstone on February 11, 2024, with Nico Hülkenberg driving. The team heads into the season with drivers Kevin Magnussen and Nico Hülkenberg for the second consecutive year and a new team principal, Ayao Komatsu, who replaced Guenther Steiner. Despite the launch, the team expressed realistic expectations, with Komatsu suggesting they might be 'towards the back of the grid, if not last' at the start of the season. <9> Formula One Management (FOM) officially announced its rejection of Andretti Global's bid to join the Formula 1 grid as an eleventh team for either the 2025 or 2026 seasons. In a detailed statement, F1 concluded that the application did not demonstrate it would add value to the championship, expressing doubts about the team's potential competitiveness. Key reasons cited included the significant challenge for a new team to build two different cars for the 2025 and the new 2026 regulations, and the concern that F1 would bring more value to the Andretti brand than the other way around. Although the FIA, motorsport's governing body, had previously approved the application from a technical standpoint, the commercial rights holder ultimately denied the entry. The door was left open for a potential entry in 2028, at which point partner General Motors plans to be ready to supply a Cadillac power unit, a factor F1 noted would lead them to view an application differently. <10> Formula One Management (FOM) officially rejected Andretti Global's bid to join the Formula 1 grid as an eleventh team for either the 2025 or 2026 seasons. The decision, announced on January 31, 2024, came after a six-month commercial assessment by F1, despite the FIA having previously approved Andretti's application in July 2023. In a detailed statement, F1 concluded that the application should not be successful primarily on the grounds that it did not believe the team would be a competitive participant or add value to the championship. F1's statement questioned Andretti's understanding of the significant challenge involved, particularly the proposal to build two different cars in its first two years of competition. Andretti Global, in partnership with Cadillac, expressed strong disagreement with the rejection, stating they were proud of the significant progress already made on a competitive car and power unit. While rejecting the 2025/2026 bid, F1 stated it would look differently on an application for the 2028 championship, especially with a full General Motors power unit.

The final approval, which resolved a long-running saga, was announced in March 2025. The entry evolved from an initial bid by Andretti Global in partnership with GM; the final approved structure is a factory Cadillac team supported by TWG Motorsports, with Michael Andretti's father, Mario Andretti, serving as an advisor. The team will initially use Ferrari power units and gearboxes before General Motors, which has registered as an F1 power unit manufacturer, develops its own works engine. This collaboration, set for the 2025 season, will feature Ramsay and his culinary team curating world-class, gourmet menus for guests within the F1 Garage, located in the paddock and pit lane. The menus will be inspired by each Grand Prix location and feature locally sourced ingredients. This partnership builds on a successful trial at the 2024 Las Vegas Grand Prix where Ramsay hosted "Ramsay's Garage". The concept builds upon the success of "Ramsay's Garage" at the 2024 Las Vegas Grand Prix, where a similar premium culinary experience was offered. [5, 6] These include F1 DRIVE, a high-performance karting experience on a portion of the actual Grand Prix circuit; F1 X, an interactive 4D exhibition with historical artifacts and racing simulators; and the F1 HUB, which contains a flagship merchandise store and dining options. These initiatives included the exclusive use of local food trucks and entertainers within fan zones to provide them with global exposure. Additionally, local artists Brett Rosepiler, Matt Murphy, and Richard Ochoa were commissioned to create Formula 1-themed murals for a pedestrian tunnel. The announcement also detailed plans for free community watch parties, which were held on Saturday, November 23, 2024, in collaboration with the City of Henderson on Water Street and at Nellis Air Force Base for active-duty military members and their families. [1]
